cards.text: The time of Abimelech is over, and Israel needs someone new. Up steps Tola son of Puah, a man from the tribe of Issachar, to save Israel. He lives in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim.

cards.question: Tola judges Israel for twenty-three years. When he dies, where is he buried?

cards.text: Next comes Jair the Gileadite, a man from Gilead. He judges Israel for twenty-two years.

cards.question: Jair has thirty sons, and they ride on thirty donkeys. How many towns do Jair's sons have in Gilead?

cards.text: Thirty sons, thirty donkeys, thirty towns, and those towns are called Havvoth-jair to this day. Friend, I could never get six cookie cutters to line up on one counter, and this man has a MATCHING SET.
When Jair dies, he's buried in Kamon. And then comes the word nobody wants to see in Judges: again.

cards.question: Once again, the Israelites do evil in the sight of the LORD. What do they serve?

answers.text: The Baals and the gods of many nations

cards.text: The Baals, the Ashtoreths, the gods of Aram, Sidon and Moab, and the gods of the Ammonites and Philistines. Friend, that's not wandering off, that's signing up for EVERY loyalty card in town.

cards.question: Along with all those other gods, the Israelites keep serving the LORD too.

cards.text: So the anger of the LORD burns against Israel. He sells them into the hands of two nations at once.

cards.question: The LORD sells Israel into the hands of which two nations?
Starting that very year, the Philistines and Ammonites harass and oppress the Israelites in Gilead for ___ years.

cards.text: Eighteen years of the Philistines and Ammonites pushing Israel around in Gilead. Then the Ammonites cross the Jordan to fight Judah, Benjamin and the house of Ephraim too.

cards.question: Israel is in deep distress. What do the Israelites do?

answers.text: They cry out to the LORD

cards.text: And they don't dress it up. They say, “We have sinned against You, for we have indeed forsaken our God and served the Baals.”
Then the LORD replies. He names the nations that oppressed them before: the Egyptians, Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines, Sidonians, Amalekites and Maonites.

cards.question: The LORD names the nations that oppressed Israel before. What does He say happened when Israel cried out to Him?

answers.text: He saved them from their hands
He left them there for good
He sent them a king instead

cards.question: But now Israel has forsaken the LORD and served other gods. What does the LORD say He will do?

cards.text: Then He says, “Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them save you in your time of trouble.” Friend. Let that one sit for a second.

cards.question: After the LORD tells them to cry out to the gods they've chosen, how do the Israelites answer Him?

answers.text: They confess again and beg Him
They go cry out to the Baals
They argue they never left Him

cards.text: They tell the LORD, “We have sinned,” and then, “Deal with us as You see fit; but please deliver us today!” I bet after eighteen years, TODAY was the only word that mattered.

cards.question: Words are one thing. What do the Israelites do with the foreign gods among them?

answers.text: They hide them in their tents

cards.question: Once the Israelites serve the LORD again, He can no longer bear the misery of Israel.

cards.text: Then the Ammonites are called to arms and camp in Gilead. The Israelites gather and camp at Mizpah.

cards.question: The rulers of Gilead talk it over with one another. What do they say whoever launches the attack against the Ammonites will become?

answers.text: Head of all who live in Gilead

cards.text: Two armies camped and a top job sitting open, and nobody's stepped up yet. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story is just getting started.

findings.problem: Abimelech appears for the first time here and is never introduced. The baker isn't told who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Judges 10:1-5 is a run of minor-judge notices: names, years judged, burial places, sons, donkeys and towns. Little happens in it. It gets six cards here, and cards 2 and 4 quiz details from it (Tola's burial place and the number of Jair's towns). It should be summed up in one story card with no choice cards. It can still name a standout detail, like Jair's thirty sons on thirty donkeys.

rule.text: If a stretch is mostly detail and not much happens, it counts.

findings.problem: This choice card asks how many towns Jair's sons have. That is a detail from the minor-judge stretch in Judges 10:1-5, which should not get choice cards.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. "The Baals and the gods of many nations" is noticeably longer and broader than the other two answers. The word "Only" in "Only the gods of Egypt" also flags that answer as the odd one out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: This card retells the eighteen years of oppression from Judges 10:8. Stop 1 already told that, and its last choice card asked about it. The card cites Judges 10:8-9, which reaches back outside this stop's range (Judges 10:9-18). It should tell only verse 9.

"Once the Israelites serve the LORD again, He can no longer bear the misery" turns the second event into a result of the first. Judges 10:16 only joins the two with "and." It does not say how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has no real laugh lines. Its story cards ("they don't dress it up," "Let that one sit for a second," "a top job sitting open") read as pleasant narration. Some lighter moments could carry a laugh without touching God's words, such as Israel gathering at Mizpah, or the rulers of Gilead offering the top job with no one stepping up.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
